_comment: Mutation sweep for V-BRK-030 -- the agent pod's rendered KUBEAGENTS_AGENT_IDENTITY equals the identity its broker assembles from the flags it is started with. Run: python3 dev/mutate.py verification/mutants/V-BRK-030.json. Every row names the test that must fail; see dev/mutate.py for why rc != 0 is not a catch. M8 was originally 'a duplicate entry is rendered'; it is removed rather than strengthened against, because mergeEnvVars keys its override list by name and structurally cannot emit two entries of one name -- the mutation expressed no defect, so scoring it either way would have been a lie about coverage.

mutants.why: The state the repo was in before this unit. The pod knows AGENT_TIER and nothing else, so it cannot compute a key the broker will accept and 06 SS4.1's builder refuses to default one. This is the whole reason the unit exists; a check that does not catch it is not the check.

The half-identity. AGENT_TIER already exists and is identical for every developer-team agent, so an identity built from the tier alone collides two agents in the broker's dedup index -- and looks entirely plausible in a golden file.

The LSN-036/LSN-041 shape, and the reason the test composes through the production formatter. `tier + "/" + leaf` agrees with Identity.AgentIdentity() for every tier that HAS a scope; it diverges only on the empty-scope arm, where it renders `platform/` and every key computed against it is refused. A test that hand-joined the two halves would agree with this mutant.

Leaf() is namespace-then-cluster-then-project; the project is the level a reader most easily assumes. For a developer-team agent this renders the project where the broker was started with the namespace -- the two sides disagree while each looks individually sane.

brokerArgs calls agentindex.EffectiveTier; reading spec.Tier raw agrees with it for every CR that sets a tier and diverges for one that does not -- where the broker starts as `platform` and the pod is told the empty string. Defaulting that happens in two places has to happen the same way in both.

The five broker vars are appended AFTER mergeEnvVars precisely so spec.deployment.env cannot win. Rendered in the general block instead, the identity keeps its correct default and becomes settable -- and a CR author who sets it makes every write from that agent refused, a denial of service authored in a field that reads as configuration.

The drift direction the join exists for, driven from the OTHER end. Nothing here touches the agent side; the broker's --scope changes and the two renderings part company. A check that only asserted the pod's value against a literal would still be green.

M5's mirror, driven from the other end. brokerArgs stops calling agentindex.EffectiveTier, so a CR with no explicit tier starts its broker as the empty string while the pod is told `platform`. Same divergence, opposite origin -- and a check that only ever varied the agent side would be green on it.
